title: Preserve structured caller conversations and tools on cloud provider routes
goal: Carry the normalized caller chat payload through GEMI's discovered-provider route and translate OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic tool calls back to the existing caller envelope without executing them in Core.

results.implementation: Added the object-safe Provider::generate_with_chat seam, preserved normalized caller messages and tool schemas on OpenAI-compatible routes, translated the same payload to Anthropic Messages, and normalized provider tool_use/tool_calls into CALLER_TOOL_CALLS without executing them. Legacy completions, Gemini and Triton remain prompt-only. Test-only GEMI coverage moved out of the shipped source count to keep the pillar ceiling line-neutral.
results.acceptance: cargo test --offline --locked -p susi-gemi --lib cloud_provider_tool_contract -- --nocapture: 2 passed, 0 failed; cargo test --offline --locked -p susi-gemi --lib --quiet: 438 passed, 0 failed; cargo test --offline --locked -p susi-core --lib --quiet: 502 passed, 0 failed; cargo test --offline --locked -p susi-adapters-llm --lib --quiet: 21 passed, 0 failed; cargo test --offline --locked -p susi --test lean_core_ceilings -- --nocapture: 2 passed, 0 failed.
results.gate: SUSI_LOCAL_TEST_RUNNER=serial cargo run --offline --locked -p xtask --bin local-workflow -- check: passed in 146.8s; cargo fmt 3.7s, clippy 2.3s, affected cargo test 140.8s; 19 affected packages, all affected suites, GMCP requirements, guards and doc-tests passed.
results.ceiling: lean-core: susi-gemi src 20758 lines against ceiling 21096; all pillar source and dependency-reach checks passed with no ceiling increase.
results.dependencies: No Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock changes; no new third-party dependency; no credentials or live provider calls used.

limitations: OpenAI-compatible chat and Anthropic Messages are translated; legacy completions, Gemini and Triton remain prompt-only until their native tool contracts are separately verified.
Cloud credentials and live provider calls are not used by the tests; exact native-host qualification remains a separate release concern.
